gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TechGearLab's Blink Outdoor 4 test (Sentry Kelly, 2025-06-13) caught motion at 2, 5 and 10 ft but missed it at 15 and 20 ft, and that on alkaline AAs under constant motion the camera died in four days. That is the camera the Wasserstein case is built around.
standout_why: Reviewed (cited, 2026-11-06) tested twelve all-in-one feeders. It reports no measurements for the Birdfy Cam 2 line, the Wasserstein case or Blink, and mentions Blink only for privacy zones. Its only measured-style figures are Harymor's 78 pings in one day and one wrong ID. The visible part of Digital Camera World's guide (Lauren Scott, 2026-10-09) gives specs only, with no battery, ID-accuracy or detection figures, and no Wasserstein or Birdfy Cam entry. I could not open WIRED (cited), so I can't rule out that it has a Blink battery figure. That is the reason for a 2, not a 3.
decides: This supports the case-plus-Blink route only with caveats. Bird motion inside the Wasserstein case is well within the 2 ft range where TechGearLab saw detection work. But a feeder triggers constantly, and on alkaline AAs that drained the Blink in four days. The page should say to use lithium AAs only and to expect to take the feeder down to swap cells far sooner than Blink's two-year claim. This favours the Birdfy Cam 2 4K (9,000 mAh plus built-in solar) for anyone who doesn't want to keep swapping batteries. I found no named measurement of either Birdfy Cam 2 model, so nothing measured separates the Cam 2 4K from the Cam 2K.
candidates: Wasserstein Bird Feeder Camera Case + Blink Outdoor 4

findings.label: Motion detection range (TechGearLab test)
findings.value: Detected at 2, 5 and 10 ft; missed at 15 and 20 ft
findings.source_title: Blink Outdoor 4 review – TechGearLab (Sentry Kelly, with Benjamin Hickok and Kolby Anderson; published 2025-06-13)
findings.note: TechGearLab's distance walk test. In the Wasserstein case the bird sits a few inches from the lens, well inside the range that worked.

findings.label: Battery life on alkaline AAs under constant motion (TechGearLab test)
findings.source_title: Blink Outdoor 4 review – TechGearLab (Sentry Kelly, published 2025-06-13)
findings.note: TechGearLab put alkaline cells in the camera with constant motion and it lasted four days. It agrees with Blink that only lithium AAs should be used. It estimates 'a little over a month' on the standard two-battery setup, but that is an extrapolation and not a measured lithium run. It says some more efficient battery cameras it tested lasted three times as long.

findings.label: TechGearLab overall score and rank
findings.value: 57/100, ranked 18th of 20 security cameras (video 6.1, monitoring 4.7, ease of use 6.4)
findings.note: Weighted scores: video 50%, monitoring 35%, ease of use 15%. It names low-light footage as a weakness.

findings.label: Close-focus observation (Digital Camera World test with Ring Stick Up)
findings.value: Birds landed closer than the Ring camera's nearest focusing distance
findings.source_title: Wasserstein Bird Feeder Smart Case review: Bird watching made easy? – Digital Camera World (Adam Juniper, 2023-04-04)
findings.note: This is an observation, not a number. Juniper tested only a Ring Stick Up. The same review weighs the case at 1 kg (2.2 lb), rates its maximum load at 2 kg (4.4 lb), and gives the Ring's field of view as 150° and the Blink Outdoor's as 110°.
